synopsis: ISO 6165 names and classifies earth-moving machines, including loaders, excavators, dozers, dumpers and graders; ISO 20474-1:2017 and Parts 2–15 provide their baseline general and machine-specific safety requirements, with EN 474 serving as the European counterpart [f15239, f2189, f15243]. These baseline standards are not automatic-braking acceptance standards or performance matrices: braking evidence must instead come from ISO 21815, ISO 19014 and the safety case [f2190, f2720, f15248]. ISO 19014 is the sector-specific functional-safety framework for ISO 6165 machines, but projects spanning surface and underground machines must check applicability machine by machine rather than assume it for mining machines outside that classification [f2196, f2351, f15249]. There is a scope tension: one glossary entry makes ISO 6165 inclusion determinative for ISO 21815-1 applicability, while another says ISO 21815 also covers underground mining machines under ISO 19296 and road-construction machines [f15240, f15140]. Great Britain designated the EN 474:2022 family on 8 August 2026, providing a presumption-of-conformity route under the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008, but the attributed notice number 0139/26 was not confirmed [f15244, f2875]. Presumption of conformity is limited to the standard's scope, and harmonisation of EN 474 or EN ISO 21815 under Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 remained unverified while the list was being prepared in 2026 [f15080, f2209, f15081].
